Renovation
rĕn-ō-vā´shŭn
n. (renewal; the making new again of what has decayed — the Spirit's work of restoring the divine image in man)
Latin renovare, to make new again, from novus, new. The older divines use renovation where we say renewal, and pair it with regeneration as the beginning and the continuing of one work.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Renovation is the Spirit's making new. It begins at regeneration: God saved us “by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost” (Tit 3:5). It continues daily: “though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day” (2Co 4:16). It works at the level of the mind: “be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind” (Rom 12:2); “be renewed in the spirit of your mind” (Eph 4:23). And its pattern is the image it restores: “the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him” (Col 3:10).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines renovation as the act of renewing; a making new after decay, destruction or depravation; renewal; and, in theology, renovation is the change of heart wrought by the Holy Spirit.

RENOVATION, n. The act of renewing; a making new after decay, destruction or depravation; renewal; as the renovation of the heart by grace.

RENOVATE, v.t. To renew; to restore to the first state, or to a good state, after decay, destruction or depravation.

Key Scripture

Tit 3:5 — "Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;"

2Co 4:16 — "For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day."

Rom 12:2 — "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God."

Eph 4:23 — "And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;"

Col 3:10 — "And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:"

Modern Corruption

Renewal is expected as an event and given as a process, and the daily kind is the sort Scripture promises.

expand to see more

The word most often reaches Christians attached to a crisis — a conference, a decision, a season of revival — and Scripture's own adverb is day by day. Second Corinthians 4:16 sets the renewal against a decline running the other way: though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day. Both verbs are present and continuous, and the sentence assumes that a believer may be getting visibly worse in one respect while genuinely improving in another. That is an unglamorous doctrine and a merciful one, because it means an ageing or ill or exhausted Christian is not thereby a declining one.

Romans 12:2 locates the work where the modern church rarely looks for it: the mind. Be not conformed to this world, but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind — and the purpose clause follows, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God. Discernment is downstream of a renewed mind rather than a separate gift, which is why the believer who wants to know God's will is pointed first to how he thinks. Conformity to the age happens at the level of assumptions, mostly unnoticed, and is undone the same way.

Colossians 3:10 gives the pattern and it settles what renovation is aiming at: the new man is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him. Sanctification is not the manufacture of something unprecedented but the restoration of what man was made to be and lost, and the finished form of it is Christ, the image of the invisible God. The Reformed have kept regeneration and renovation distinct without separating them — the first is monergistic, instantaneous and never repeated; the second is the Spirit's continuing work in which the believer is commanded to labour, put off, put on, and be renewed.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek anakainosis (G342), renewing; anakainoo (G341), to renew; palingenesia (G3824), regeneration; metamorphoo (G3339), to transform.

expand to see more

Greek anakainosis (G342) — renewing; Titus 3:5, Romans 12:2 — both occurrences.

Greek anakainoo (G341) — to renew; 2 Corinthians 4:16, Colossians 3:10.

Greek palingenesia (G3824) — regeneration; Titus 3:5, Matthew 19:28 — of a man, and of the world.

Usage

"“The inward man is renewed day by day” — while the outward man perishes."

"“Transformed by the renewing of your mind” — discernment is downstream of it."

"“After the image of him that created him” — restoration, not invention."
